# Eliza Andrews

## Overview

- **Age:** 57 years old  <sub>[v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P29](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0029)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_

## Appearance

_Not yet known._

## Personality

Eliza Andrews is a naturally pessimistic woman whose gloomy outlook on life is well known to those around her. Described as looking even grimmer than usual, she nevertheless maintains a deep affection for her husband.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P60](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0060), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P24](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0024), [v2 XVII A Chapter of Accidents P64](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0064), [v2 XXII Odds and Ends P12](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0012)_

## History

Eliza Andrews lived with her sister Catherine in a small brown house situated in a sunny corner of Mark Andrew's beech woods. Described as grim, she and her optimistic sister were among the eccentric [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) neighbors visited by [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) while the pair canvassed their assigned road to raise funds for the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village Improvement Society's hall-painting project.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P0](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0000), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P10](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0010), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P12](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0012), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014)_

## Quotes

> "I don’t see the necessity. We didn’t gad about to halls and places when we were young, Catherine Andrews. This world is getting worse every day."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P18](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0018)

> "Doctors always talk like that just to keep people cheered up. I wouldn’t have much hope if I was her. It’s best to be prepared for the worst."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P27](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0027)

> “You think!” Miss Eliza’s voice expressed the utmost contempt. “It doesn’t signify what you think, Catherine Andrews. Facts is facts.”
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P20](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0020)

> "set fire to her aunt’s carded rolls."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P8](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0008)

> "There isn’t any bright side."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P22](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0022)
